concepts.name: Scarcity and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Explain that unlimited wants meet limited resources, so every choice requires giving something up.

concepts.name: Opportunity cost
concepts.summary: Identify the value of the best forgone alternative in a simple everyday or business choice.

concepts.name: Demand and law of demand
concepts.summary: Describe how quantity demanded falls as price rises, other things equal, and read a demand schedule or curve.

concepts.name: Supply and law of supply
concepts.summary: Describe how quantity supplied rises with price and read a supply schedule or curve.

concepts.name: Market equilibrium price
concepts.summary: Locate the price where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded and explain why surpluses and shortages push prices toward it.

concepts.name: Marginal thinking
concepts.summary: Recognise that rational choices compare the extra benefit and extra cost of one more unit.

concepts.name: Positive versus normative statements
concepts.summary: Distinguish testable statements about what is from value judgements about what ought to be.

misconceptions.text: Scarcity only affects poor people or poor countries.
Opportunity cost is the total of all money spent on a choice.
A shortage means a good has completely run out.

concepts.name: Shifts versus movements
aliases: change in demand vs quantity demanded
concepts.summary: Apply the distinction between a price-driven movement along a curve and a non-price shift of the curve.

concepts.name: Determinants of demand and supply
concepts.summary: Use income, related goods, tastes, input costs and technology to predict which curve shifts and in which direction.

concepts.name: Comparative statics of equilibrium
concepts.summary: Predict the new equilibrium price and quantity after a shift in one curve or both.

concepts.name: Price elasticity of demand
concepts.summary: Calculate and interpret elasticity from price and quantity changes, classifying demand as elastic, inelastic or unit elastic.

concepts.name: Elasticity and total revenue
concepts.summary: Apply elasticity to predict how a price change alters a seller's revenue.

concepts.name: Price ceilings and floors
concepts.summary: Show how binding price controls create shortages or surpluses in a supply and demand diagram.

concepts.name: Consumer and producer surplus
concepts.summary: Measure the benefit buyers and sellers receive as areas under demand and above supply.

misconceptions.text: A higher price shifts the demand curve to the left.
Elasticity is the same as the slope of the demand curve.
Raising price always increases a firm's revenue.

concepts.name: Utility maximisation and budget constraint
concepts.summary: Derive a consumer's optimal bundle by equating marginal utility per dollar across goods given income and prices.

concepts.name: Short-run production and diminishing returns
concepts.summary: Analyse how output responds to additional variable input when some inputs are fixed.

concepts.name: Cost curves
concepts.summary: Derive and relate fixed, variable, average and marginal costs, including why MC crosses average curves at their minima.

concepts.name: Profit maximisation rule
concepts.summary: Determine the profit-maximising output where marginal revenue equals marginal cost and when a firm should shut down.

concepts.name: Perfect competition outcomes
concepts.summary: Analyse how price-taking firms, entry and exit drive long-run price to minimum average cost.

concepts.name: Monopoly pricing and deadweight loss
concepts.summary: Explain why a monopolist sets MR = MC, charges above marginal cost and causes deadweight loss.

concepts.name: Other elasticities
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret income, cross-price and supply elasticities to classify goods and predict responses.

concepts.name: Tax incidence
concepts.summary: Analyse how the burden of a tax splits between buyers and sellers according to relative elasticities.

misconceptions.text: A firm should produce where average cost is lowest to maximise profit.
Monopolists can charge any price they like and still sell the same quantity.
The party legally required to pay a tax is the one who bears its burden.

concepts.name: Long-run costs and scale
concepts.summary: Analyse how returns to scale and the long-run average cost curve determine efficient firm size and market structure.

concepts.name: Price discrimination
concepts.summary: Evaluate when and how firms with market power charge different prices to different customers and the welfare effects.

concepts.name: Monopolistic competition
concepts.summary: Analyse firms with differentiated products, free entry, excess capacity and zero long-run profit.

concepts.name: Oligopoly and game theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate strategic interaction among few firms using Nash equilibrium and why collusion is unstable.

concepts.name: Externalities and Pigouvian remedies
concepts.summary: Evaluate how divergence between private and social cost or benefit causes inefficiency and compare taxes, subsidies and regulation.

concepts.name: Public goods and common resources
concepts.summary: Analyse non-rivalry and non-excludability and why markets under-provide public goods and over-use common resources.

concepts.name: Asymmetric information
concepts.summary: Analyse how hidden information or action distorts markets such as insurance and used goods.

concepts.name: Factor markets and wages
concepts.summary: Analyse how firms hire inputs where marginal revenue product equals factor price and how wages are set.

misconceptions.text: Oligopoly firms always collude because it maximises joint profit.
Any externality should be eliminated entirely.
Price discrimination always harms consumers and lowers total welfare.

concepts.name: Coase theorem and property rights
concepts.summary: Judge when private negotiation can resolve externalities and why transaction costs and unclear rights limit it.

concepts.name: Mechanism design and auctions
concepts.summary: Design rules or auction formats that elicit truthful information and achieve a stated objective.

concepts.name: Contracts and principal-agent incentives
concepts.summary: Design contracts or signals that align incentives under hidden information or hidden action.

concepts.name: Welfare analysis and distribution
concepts.summary: Critique policies using Pareto and compensation criteria while weighing efficiency against equity.

concepts.name: Comparing remedies for market failure
concepts.summary: Evaluate corrective taxes, tradable permits, regulation and bargaining under uncertainty and transaction costs.

concepts.name: Government failure and second best
concepts.summary: Assess when intervention worsens outcomes because of information limits, incentives or other existing distortions.

concepts.name: Competition policy and market definition
concepts.summary: Evaluate mergers and conduct using concentration, substitutes, entry barriers and consumer welfare effects.

concepts.name: Behavioural departures from rationality
concepts.summary: Evaluate where systematic biases undermine standard choice models and how this changes market and policy design.

misconceptions.text: The Coase theorem shows markets always solve externalities without government.
Fixing one market distortion always moves the economy closer to efficiency.
A Pareto-efficient outcome is necessarily fair.
